questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes policy-as-code skills, Istio security posture, and CI/CD integration. It tests ability to craft minimal, verifiable manifests and to reason about runtime vs CI checks.

## Key Concepts

- Istio PeerAuthentication mtls: STRICT
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno policy or alternative
- CI validation: lint, dry-run apply, policy testing
- Runtime enforcement: Istio sidecars enforce mTLS

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8smtlstrict
spec:
  crd:
    Spec:
      groups: ["constraints.gatekeeper.sh"]
      names:
        kind: K8sMTLSStrict
        plural: k8smTLSStricts
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8smtlstrict
        violation["mtls_missing"] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Namespace"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["istio-injection"]
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sMTLSStrict
metadata:
  name: mtls-strict
spec:
  match:
    requiredImages: []
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: PeerAuthentication with mtls: STRICT
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: missing PeerAuthentication
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample
  namespace: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
```

- How would you enable gradual rollout for mTLS enforcement?
- What exceptions would you permit and how would you audit them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world security requires automated SBOMs and multi-tool vulnerability checks to prevent risky images from entering registries.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- Parallel scans with Trivy and Grype
- PR gating and artifact attachment
- Validation in CI and via PR comments

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions workflow (yaml)
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t myimage:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock anchore/syft:latest DockerImage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Scan with Trivy
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock aquasecurity/trivy:latest image --exit-code 1 --no-progress myimage:${{ github.sha }} || true
      - name: Scan with Grype
        run: |
          grype myimage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > grype.json || true
      - name: Upload SBOMs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sboms
          path: sbom.json, grype.json
      - name: Fail if CVEs found
        run: |
          if [ -s grype.json ] && grep -q '"score": 7' grype.json; then exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this gate for a multi-arch build?
- How would you integrate SBOM attestation into your registry metadata?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design progressive delivery gates at scale, with multi-cloud constraints and real-world SLO-based rollouts; focuses on policy, tooling (Argo Rollouts, Prometheus), and CI integration; evaluates trade-offs between safety and speed, failure modes; ensures observability and reproducibility.

## Key Concepts

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for promotion failure modes if the AnalysisTemplate temporarily becomes unavailable?
- How would you adapt this gate for multi-tenant environments with separate SLIs per tenant?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests end-to-end security design for multi-cloud Kubernetes workloads, focusing on identity, secret management, and policy enforcement with real-world tools.

## Key Concepts
- Zero-trust workload identity (SPIRE)
- Ephemeral credentials (Vault)
- Service mesh security (Istio, mTLS, AuthorizationPolicies)
- Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego)
- Egress controls to data lake and namespace isolation

## Sample Solution

### 1. SPIRE Workload Identity
```yaml
# spire-workload.yaml
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: data-platform-workload
spec:
  names:
    - data-service
    - analytics-service
    - etl-service
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: production
```

### 2. Vault Integration for Secrets
```yaml
# vault-secret-store.yaml
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultSecret
metadata:
  name: data-lake-credentials
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  vaultAddress: https://vault.data-platform.svc.cluster.local:8200
  path: secret/data-lake
  provider: hcp
  refreshInterval: 1h
```

### 3. Istio AuthorizationPolicy
```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run OPA policy check
        run: |
          opa eval --fail-defined-deny \
            --data policy.rego \
            --input manifests/
```

## Key Takeaways
- SPIRE provides cryptographically secure workload identity
- Vault enables dynamic secret rotation without application changes
- Istio mTLS ensures service-to-service encryption
- OPA/Rego enforces admission control and runtime policies

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Why this angle matters: binds image attestation, SBOM, secret management, and canary verification across clouds, aligning with production-grade trust.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore cosign attestation
- SBOM requirements
- SecretStore-based injection
- Kyverno/OPA admission gates
- Canary release with Prometheus SLOs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sigstore-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: audit
  rules:
  - name: attest-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, StatefulSet]
    validate:
      message: "image must be cosigned and SBOM present"
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]: "*"
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"]: "*"
```

```rego
# OPA policy (high level)
package gatekeeper
violation[{"msg": msg}]
default violation = []
violation = [{"msg": m} |
  input.request.kind == "Deployment" and
  not input.request.object.spec.template.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]
  or not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"] ]
```
